title: Restoring ability to remove zombie cells may keep us sharp as we age | New Scientist
description: Zombie, or senescent, cells accumulate in our body with age, when we become less able to clear them. But a study in mice suggests that a drug could restore this ability and improve ageing outcomes
author: Isha Ishtiaq

title: Neurostimulation restores feeling in paralysed hand for months after | New Scientist
description: Keith Thomas, 48, has paralysis, but brain stimulation helped him regain some feeling and movement in his hands – and this was maintained even when the stimulation was turned off
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: We’ve found a rocky, temperate planet’s atmosphere for the first time | New Scientist
description: Astronomers have only previously found atmospheres around exoplanets that are very large or incredibly hot – but now they have found one adorning a world that may well be right for life
author: Leah Crane

title: Next-generation Alzheimer's drug reduces risk of serious brain bleeds | New Scientist
description: A new kind of antibody drug that more efficiently enters the brain could slow the progression of Alzheimer's disease with a much lower risk of dangerous side effects than existing therapies
author: Carissa Wong

title: Stealth drone spins so fast that it disappears | New Scientist
description: A drone that spins 25 times a second can avoid being spotted by becoming nothing more than a vague blur – though the creators admit that it can still be easily heard
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: Congolese monkey with mask-like face and strong BO is new to science | New Scientist
description: A black colobus monkey from a remote part of the Congo Basin rainforest, known locally as likweli, is thought to be severely threatened by poaching
author: James Woodford
